analysis:
Compared the complete supplied BASE/HEAD DaemonStateFile.swift source. Changes add optional startup/switch model filters and recovery diagnostics (head 54–70), initializer parameters and assignments (374–378, 413–417). Optional fields preserve decoding of older snapshots; schema validation, atomic best-effort writes, process identity, trust/authorization reporting and slot/cache posture remain unchanged (head 658–676). No supported new exposure of prompts, private keys or credentials, authorization bypass, billing change or cache-isolation regression appears in this file. Existing file-access behavior is not a new finding.
Examined SelectedModelRecovery.swift addition metadata and its bounded patch: backoff is 30–600 seconds, victim minimum idle is 120 seconds and residency-transition recheck is 15 seconds (head 9–17); entries use ContinuousClock scheduling and track an asynchronous attempt. Most of its 101-line implementation and its ProviderLoop integration are not supplied. These limits prevent a conclusion about recovery availability behavior, rather than establish a missing control.
Integration should examine recovery producers/consumers, task cancellation and load/eviction admission, particularly preservation of add-on hold/model-load fencing (A-018, TB-012, T-059), pending-work exclusions and idle behavior (T-010, T-029), and authorization validity during delayed work (T-053). Verify SelectedModelRecoveryEntry serialization does not introduce sensitive request-derived diagnostics. Nothing visible changes T-041 cache cryptography, scope or TTL; model reload effects must be checked in the supplied integration scope. No concrete regression is established locally.
